clue.text: Young insects raised up on pea soup

indicators.note: in a down clue something raised is turned upward, so the little word up is read bottom to top
a soup is a mixture, so the letters of pea are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Some young bugs have climbed onto a bowl of pea soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just sets one piece beside the other; read in a down clue, 'raised up' looks like a lifted spoon but is the turning signal plus its word.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects in the chrysalis stage between larva and adult are immature forms, hence young.

clue.text: Found note in packing case

indicators.note: the note sits in the packing case, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a crate is a wooden packing case

explanation.surface: Someone discovered a letter tucked inside a shipping crate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' looks like the past tense of find; here it is the verb meaning establish.
explanation.definitionFit: To found an institution is to establish or bring it into being, a synonym.

clue.text: Traditional drinks are a sell out

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Traditional beverages are so popular they have sold out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges ARE A SELL into the eight letters needed; 'sell out' reads as a phrase meaning a sell-out success.
explanation.definitionFit: Cask-conditioned beers brewed the old way are championed in Britain as traditional drinks.

clue.text: Child that is dressed up for Gaelic gathering

indicators.note: dressed up suggests a disguise, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A child in fancy dress for a Scottish social evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressed up' shuffles CHILD plus IE into one word. A ceilidh is a Scottish or Irish evening of folk dancing and music.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional Scottish or Irish social event with music and dancing, a party gathering.

clue.text: Meet a number on the border

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
a verge is a grassy border of a road

explanation.surface: Gather at a number painted on the roadside edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a number' is the Roman numeral C, not ONE; VERGE is the strip of grass beside a British road.
explanation.definitionFit: To converge is to come together from different directions, as people do when they assemble.

clue.text: Skinny, toothless what's-his-name

parts.note: with no teeth one shows only gums, so gummy

explanation.surface: Describes a thin man with no teeth whose name escapes you.
explanation.definitionFit: A placeholder word for a person or thing whose name one has forgotten.

clue.text: Put up or cut up

explanation.surface: Lodged somewhere, or chopped into pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers billeted in lodgings are housed there; something divided into four parts has been chopped into pieces.

clue.text: Coffee for a short time, then tea

parts.note: cha is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: Order a coffee for a quick break, then have a cuppa.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine type of coffee, originally shipped from the Yemeni port of that name.

clue.text: Just for the record,500 is over 100

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece over another simply comes before it

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A remark that, for the record, five hundred exceeds one hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: Roman numerals: D is 500 and C is 100.
explanation.definitionFit: A gramophone record is a flat round platter of vinyl, a synonym.

clue.text: Corresponding but never meeting

explanation.surface: Two things that match yet never touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Analogous things correspond closely; geometric lines running side by side never intersect.

clue.text: When in a hole, use your ingenuity

parts.note: a vent is a hole letting air or gas out

explanation.surface: Advice that, when stuck in trouble, you should think creatively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a hole' looks like the idiom for trouble; it is IN plus a synonym for hole.
explanation.definitionFit: To devise something new is to apply cleverness and originality.

clue.text: Inventor of the telephone — or part of it

explanation.surface: The man credited with the telephone, or a component of one.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Graham, the Scot credited with the telephone; old phones also had a ringer to signal calls.

clue.text: Break our codes in a conventional way

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase for an adjective: behaving in a conventional way

indicators.note: break means smash apart, so the letters are shattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: A spy cracks our ciphers by perfectly orthodox means.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break' rearranges OUR CODES; it reads as code-breaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorous behaviour is proper and in keeping with polite good taste and convention.

clue.text: Ground and house might be theirs

definitions.text: Ground and house might be theirs

parts.note: the Lords is the upper house of the British Parliament

explanation.surface: Property owners might own both the land and the building.
explanation.walkthrough: The House of Lords is the upper chamber of Britain's Parliament. The whole clue also defines: owners of land and houses.
explanation.definitionFit: People who own property and let it to tenants might own both the plot and the building.

clue.text: Service initiation

explanation.surface: A church rite that also marks a first experience.
explanation.definitionFit: A Christian rite with water is a church ceremony; a first hard experience is a figurative baptism of fire.

clue.text: Getting out stupidly in Test is a sort of lesson

indicators.note: the jumbled word is placed in the test, so one piece goes inside the other
something done stupidly is muddled, so the letters of out are rearranged

explanation.surface: A batsman getting out foolishly in a cricket Test match teaches a lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting' and 'is' are link words. A Test is an international cricket match, which is why getting out stupidly fits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A small-group teaching session with a tutor is one kind of class.

clue.text: Academic groups selected-by new masters?

indicators.note: new signals the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Asks whether classes of pupils are picked by newly arrived teachers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges MASTERS. British schools often stream pupils into classes by ability.
explanation.definitionFit: Ability-based class sets in a British school are the divisions into which pupils are sorted.

clue.text: Dancers on tour

explanation.surface: Performers out travelling.
explanation.definitionFit: To trip is to step lightly as in dancing; holidaymakers on a day out are also so called.

clue.text: Hoped to rise from despair

indicators.note: from here means made out of, so the letters of despair are rebuilt into a new word

explanation.surface: Someone longed to climb out of hopelessness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' tells you to build the answer out of the letters of DESPAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to have ambitions to climb higher, so hoping to rise matches.

clue.text: Tricked into side issues

indicators.note: tricked means fooled about with, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone was conned into irrelevant side matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tricked' rearranges INTO SIDE; 'issues' looks like topics but means printings.
explanation.definitionFit: Each printed version of a newspaper or magazine is a separate publication.

clue.text: This oven has a ring outside for roasting

indicators.note: the word roasting wraps the answer in a ring of its own outer letters, so the answer sits concealed in its middle

explanation.surface: An oven with a ring around it is used for roasting.
explanation.walkthrough: In ROASTING the R in front and ING behind together spell RING, the ring outside the answer. An oast is a kiln for drying hops.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiln used in Kent for drying hops is a kind of oven.

clue.text: Letter without a beginning produces irritation

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: aitch is the spelt-out name of the letter H

explanation.surface: A letter missing its opening line causes annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' is a letter of the alphabet, spelt out as its name.
explanation.definitionFit: An urge to scratch is a skin irritation.

clue.text: Pick a hundred socks with a hole in

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: the hole is put in the socks, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: hose is an old word for stockings or socks
O is round like a hole

explanation.surface: Select from a hundred socks with holes in them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts O inside HOSE, giving HOOSE after the C.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick is to select from options, a synonym.

clue.text: Submit to delay, perhaps

explanation.surface: Give in to postponement, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: To bow to someone's judgement is to yield to them; to put off is to postpone.

clue.text: Where rackets may be exposed

parts.note: rackets are tennis bats on show at tennis venues, and criminal schemes revealed in a law trial

explanation.surface: A place where swindles are revealed.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis venues display rackets; law tribunals uncover criminal scams.

clue.text: I am conclusively shown to be better

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am

explanation.surface: Someone declares they have been demonstrated to be superior.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made better has been enhanced, a synonym in past-participle form.

clue.text: Schemes thrown aside

indicators.note: thrown suggests letters tossed about and landing in a new order

explanation.surface: Plans that have been discarded.
explanation.definitionFit: Plans or notions in the mind are thoughts or proposals.

clue.text: Urge to go into action, though dispirited

indicators.note: one piece is said to go into another, so it is placed inside it

explanation.surface: Feeling pushed into action even while low in spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'though' is a link word; the surface reads 'Urge' as a noun, but it is the verb press.
explanation.definitionFit: Low in spirits and gloomy is a synonym of feeling down.
